reviewer: Codex license_audit sub-agent; independent source/Compose semantic review; no human approval or production deployment claimed
scope: Only the two new Agent-to-Java healthy startup dependencies and the directly affected VEX/vendor Compose source bindings. Root CodeQL policy is not changed by this review.
failure_evidence_boundary: Release coordinator observed daily Agent exit3 with verify_dataset -> Java connection refusal. This reviewer independently verified the startup dependency in owning source; it did not collect the initial container log.
root_cause_proof: prepare_java_deployment.py emits the same newly generated DATASET_ID for business and Agent runtime files.

Agent lifespan calls verify_dataset before yielding startup; verify_dataset performs an authenticated GET to fixed BUSINESS_URL/internal/v2/dataset and fails on a connection error or dataset mismatch. There is no bounded-retry fallback in this path.

Before this change neither application Compose file declared the Agent startup dependency on Java readiness. Starting all stopped services together can reach the dataset check before Java is listening.
acyclic_proof: Both Compose files declare backend -> postgres(service_healthy); neither backend depends_on includes Agent.
Java HealthController.ready checks SingleInstance.owned when workers are enabled and queries evidence_revision in PostgreSQL; it never calls Agent readiness or capabilities.

SingleInstance acquires/verifies its PostgreSQL advisory-lock connection. DeploymentIdentity initialization validates PostgreSQL and upload/storage dataset ownership, with local or configured object storage; it does not wait on Agent.
The added dependency is agent -> backend(service_healthy), so the core order is postgres -> backend -> agent, with frontend separately depending on backend.
The cloud-database overlay resets only backend -> local postgres. It retains agent -> backend and therefore introduces no reverse dependency or cycle.
